[[File:Silver medal of 1904 Summer Olympics.jpg|right|thumb|265px|The silver medal awarded for the 800m run during the [[1904 Summer Olympics]]]]
The [[1904 Summer Olympics]] were held in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]], [[United States]] from July 1 to November 23, 1904, as part of the [[Louisiana Purchase Exposition|St. Louis World's Fair]]. 

A total of 651&nbsp;athletes from 12&nbsp;nations participated in 95&nbsp;events in 16&nbsp;sports at these games.<ref name="olympic.org">{{cite web |title=St. Louis 1904&ndash;Games of the III Olympiad |publisher=International Olympic Committee |url=http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/index_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1904 |accessdate=August 15, 2008| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080815120301/http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/index_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1904| archivedate= August 15, 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Sullivan |first=James E. |title=Spalding's Official Athletic Almanac for 1905 |publisher=American Sports Publishing Company |date=1905 |location=New York |url=http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1904/1904Spal.pdf |page=221 |accessdate=August 15, 2008 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110829191500/http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1904/1904Spal.pdf |archive-date=August 29, 2011}}</ref>

Nine participating nations earned medals, in addition to four medals won by [[Mixed team at the Olympics|mixed team]]s. In the early Olympic Games, several team events were contested by athletes from multiple nations.<ref>{{cite web |title=1896 - Summer Olympics I (Athens, Greece) |publisher=TSN |url=https://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=9337 |accessdate=May 6, 2008|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080618213512/http://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=9337 |archivedate=June 18, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> Retroactively, the IOC created the designation "mixed team" (with the [[List of IOC country codes|country code]] ZZX) to refer to these groups of athletes. Some athletes won medals both individually and as part of a mixed team, so these medals are tabulated under different nations in the official counts.<ref name="medal count"/>

The United States won 248 medals, setting a record that still stands today. The [[Soviet Union at the Olympics|Soviet Union]] came closest to beating the record with 195 medals at the [[1980 Summer Olympics]] and currently is in second place. The Soviets briefly shared the record for gold medals with the Americans, matching the USA's 80 gold medals from 1904 with their own result at the 1980 Olympic Games. However, the United States subsequently won 83 gold medals in the [[1984 Summer Olympics]], setting another all-time record.<ref name="medal count">{{cite web |title=St. Louis 1904 – Medal Table |publisher=International Olympic Committee |url=http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/table_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1904 |accessdate=August 15, 2008| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080815084218/http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/table_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1904| archivedate= August 15, 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref> [[Gold medal]]s were awarded to event winners for the first time at the 1904 games. Prior to that, a [[silver medal]] was awarded to first-place finishers and a [[bronze medal]] to second-place finishers.<ref name="Mallon">{{cite book | author = Mallon, Bill | year = 1998 | title = The 1900 Olympic Games, Results for All Competitors in All Events, with Commentary | publisher = McFarland & Company, Inc., Publishers | location = Jefferson, North Carolina | isbn = 0-7864-0378-0 | url-access = registration | url = https://archive.org/details/1900olympicgames00mall}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last = Lucas | first = Charles J. P. | title = The Olympic Games 1904 | publisher = Woodward and Tiernan Printing Company | date = 1904 | location = St. Louis | url = http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1904/1904lucas.pdf | accessdate = August 15, 2008 <!--DASHBot--> | archive-date = March 4, 2009 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090304003336/http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1904/1904lucas.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Medal table ==
[[File:Charles Meldrum Daniels.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Charles Daniels (swimmer)|Charles Daniels]] won three gold, one silver, and one bronze medal in swimming for the United States during the 1904 games.]]

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] | date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us}}</ref>

===Reallocation of Olympic medals to club affiliation===
====IOC attribution policy====
From the [[1896 Summer Olympics|1896]] to [[1904 Summer Olympics|1904]] Olympic Games, athletes were not always entered by [[nationality]]. While many competed under their [[National Olympic Committees]] (NOCs), others were entered by [[Sports club|clubs]], particularly in [[Team sport|team events]]. In such cases, participation and medals could be attributed to the country of the club rather than the athlete's nationality.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/static/faq |title=Olympedia – FAQ Nationality |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> Consequently,The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has applied an inconsistent approach for attributing participation and medals from the 1896–1904 Olympic Games over time, alternating between the athlete's nationality and the national affiliation of the club they represented.

*'''Team events''': Until 2024, the IOC classified all teams composed of athletes from different countries in the early [[Modern Olympic Games]] as [[Mixed teams at the Olympics|mixed teams]] ([[List of IOC country codes|IOC code]] ''ZZX''), regardless of whether they represented an established club. Since 2024, teams representing a club have been attributed to the club's country, even if they included foreign athletes. Only ad hoc teams formed solely for the Olympic Games are now classified as mixed teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-1896/results/tennis/doubles-men|title=Athens 1896 doubles men Results - Olympic tennis|website=Olympics|access-date=2024-09-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240903184515/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-1896/results/tennis/doubles-men|archive-date=2024-09-03}}</ref><ref name="Medal">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/MIX|title=Mixed team at the Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=2 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502013100/http://www.olympedia.org/countries/MIX|url-status=live}}</ref>
*'''Individual events''': From 2021 to 2024, the IOC attributed medals in individual events according to the athlete's nationality, even when the athlete represented a foreign club. Since 2024, participation and medals have instead been attributed according to the national affiliation of the club represented by the athlete, largely restoring the attribution policy that had been applied for these Games prior to 2021.
<div style="visibility: hidden">&nbsp;</div>

A total of 19 medals from the 1904 Olympic Games, 16 in individual and 3 in team events, have been reallocated by the IOC since 2024. These medals have only been reallocated to two countries, 17 to the [[United States at the 1904 Summer Olympics|United States]] and 2 to [[Germany at the 1904 Summer Olympics|Germany]].

== Notes ==
{{notelist|colwidth=1|group=upper-alpha}}
{{notelist-num|refs=
{{efn-num|name=fn1|The International Olympic Committee originally considered [[Norwegian Americans|Norwegian-American]] wrestlers [[Charles Ericksen]] and [[Bernhoff Hansen]] to have competed for the United States (both were [[Norwegians|Norwegian]] immigrants to the US); each won a gold medal. In 2012, Norwegian historians however found documentation showing that Ericksen did not receive American citizenship until March 22, 1905, and that Hansen, who was registered as an "alien" (foreigner) as late as 1925, probably never received American citizenship. The historians have therefore petitioned to have the athletes registered as Norwegian.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nrk.no/ol2012/nyheter/her-er-norges-ukjente-ol-gullvinner-1.8281024|work=NRK|title=Her er beviset som endrer norsk idrettshistorie|date=14 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.svd.se/sport/usas-os-guld-var-egentligen-norges_7422064.svd|work=Svenska Dagbladet|title=USA-guld 1904 var Norges|date=14 August 2012}}</ref> In May 2013, it was reported that the [[Norwegian Olympic Committee]] had filed a formal application for changing the nationality of the wrestlers in IOC's medal database.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/kampsport/article3617871.ece|work=Nettavisen|title=Norges OL-historie skrives på nytt|date=3 May 2013|access-date=4 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212143710/http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/kampsport/article3617871.ece|archive-date=12 December 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July 2021, the IOC modified data in the official database, recognizing Ericksen and Hansen as having competed for Norway.<ref name="pre2024_wrest_heavy"/><ref name="post2024_wrest_welter"/> Since 2024, the IOC has considered the National Olympic Committee (NOC) affiliation of the team for which an athlete competed to be the decisive factor for the first three Olympic Games (1896–1904), attributing participation and medals accordingly.<ref name="post2024_wrest_heavy"/><ref name="post2024_wrest_welter"/>}}
{{efn-num|name=fn2|Representing the Philadelphia Turngemeinde at the 1904 Summer Olympics in [[St. Louis, Missouri|St. Louis]], Lenhart won the gold medal in the  [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's all-around|individual all-around]] and the silver medal in [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's triathlon|triathlon]] at the [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics|gymnastics events]].<ref name="post2024_allaround" /><ref name="post2024_triathlon" /> In addition, he also led the 'Philadelphia Turngemeinde' team to victory in the [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's team|team all-around]] competition, earning his second gold medal.<ref name="olympedia_team_apparatus"/>}}
{{efn-num|name=fn3|Born in [[Liestal]], [[Switzerland]], he represented the German gymnastics club 'Turnverein Esslingen' at the 1904 Olympic Games. Although Swiss by [[nationality]], the official entry lists identified him as competing for [[Germany at the 1904 Summer Olympics|Germany]]. Spinnler won two medals in [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics|gymnastics]], gold in the  [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's triathlon|triathlon event]] and bronze in the [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's all-around|individual all-around event]].<ref name="post2024_allaround"/><ref name="post2024_triathlon"/>}}
{{efn-num|name=fn4|The Games report refers to Corey as a "Frenchman wearing the colors of the Chicago Athletic Association".<ref>{{cite book |title=The Olympic Games — 1904 |author=Charles J.P. Lucas |publisher=Woodard & Tiernan |year=1905 |location=St. Louis, MO |url=http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1904/1904lucas.pdf |type=PDF |access-date=2007-03-27 |page=47 |archive-date=2009-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304003336/http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1904/1904lucas.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Corey was a French immigrant to the United States, who lived in the United States and did not have the right papers. The [[International Olympic Committee]] attributes his medals in the marathon and the four mile team race to the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Corey |url=https://olympics.com/en/athletes/albert-corey |website=International Olympic Committee}}</ref>}}
{{efn-num|name=fn5|For many years, it was believed that either one or two Australians had competed at the Games, with neither winning medals.<ref>{{cite book|title=A Thoroughly Unhelpful History of Australian Sport|author=Titus O'Reily|date=20 August 2018|publisher=Penguin Books|ISBN=9780143793519|page=262}}</ref> However, in 2009, it came to light that swimmer [[Francis Gailey|Frank Gailey]]; born in [[Brisbane, Queensland]], Australia; who later immigrated to the United States and became a U.S. citizen, had not yet done so when he competed at the Games, and the main reason he was wrongly identified as an American at the time was because he had joined the San Francisco Olympic club.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=St Louis 1904 |url=https://www.olympics.com.au/games/st-louis-1904/ |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=Australian Olympic Committee |language=en-AU}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web|first1=Harry|last1=Gordon|url=https://www.smh.com.au/articles/2009/02/27/1235237920406.html|title=Unveiled: our lost Olympic champion|website=Sydney Morning Herald|date=28 February 2009|accessdate=14 August 2016}}</ref> Gailey won three silver medals and one bronze medal.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Francis Gailey |url=https://www.olympics.com.au/olympians/francis-gailey/ |access-date=8 August 2024 |website=Australian Olympic Committee |language=en-AU}}</ref> The IOC counts Gailey's four medals for the [[United States at the 1904 Summer Olympics|United States]]}}
{{efn-num|name=fn6|The IOC listed [[German-American]] Franz Kugler as a member of the U.S. delegation from the beginning,<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |title=Frank Kugler |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/frank-kugler-1.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417075738/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/frank-kugler-1.html |archivedate=2020-04-17}}</ref> when it assigned the medals he had won at the 1904 St. Louis Olympics to the [[United States at the 1904 Summer Olympics|United States]].}}
{{efn-num|name=fn7|Otto Wahle was an Austrian national until 1906 when he became a [[Citizenship of the United States|US citizen]], after settling in [[New York City|New York]]. He competed for Austria at both the [[Austria at the 1900 Summer Olympics|1900]] and [[Austria at the 1904 Summer Olympics|1904]] Olympics, while being affiliated with the ''New York Athletic Club'' at the latter Games.<ref name="olympedia_wahle">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/45410|title=Olympedia – Otto Wahle |work=Olympedia |access-date=8 August 2026}}</ref> However, unlike in 1900, his bronze medal from 1904 is attributed to the United States because he competed for an American sports club.<ref name="olympics_swim400m"/>}}
{{efn-num|name=fn8|Gustav Tiefenthaler was born in Switzerland but the family moved to the United States when he was young. Tiefenthaler was still a Swiss citizen in 1904, but he represented the South Broadway Athletic Club in St. Louis, an American club.<ref name="olympedia_tiefenthaler">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/60779 |title=Olympedia – Gustav Tiefenthaler |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}
{{efn-num|name=fn9|There were 13 teams entered in this all-around team event, with gymnasts from three nations, although all teams were from American turnvereins (gymnastics clubs). The teams represented 10 American cities, including two teams from [[St. Louis]] and three from [[Chicago]]. Each team consisted of six gymnasts, with their scores from the [[Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's artistic individual all-around|individual all-around event]], with adjustments made due to predetermined maximum scores for each discipline. The gold medal was won by the Philadelphia Turngemeinde, led by [[Austrians|Austrian]] gymnast [[Julius Lenhart]], who had also won the individual all-around competition. Lenhart had only lived in [[Philadelphia]] for a few years before returning to Austria. [[Germany at the 1904 Summer Olympics|Germany]] also attempted to enter a team, but its entry was rejected because the German gymnasts were not members of the same club.<ref name="olympedia_team_apparatus">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/70024 |title=Olympedia – Team (Apparatus Work and Field Sports), Men |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}
}}
